title: College Football Playoff rankings predictions: Who will rise, fall and enter new Top 25?
content:
The top 10 teams in last week’s College Football Playoff rankings went 10-0 in Week 11. Perhaps that means there will be little movement when the new rankings are released at 9 p.m. ET Tuesday, but Indiana falling five spots after a bye showed we should be prepared to be surprised.

Each week, I use my college football projection model to predict how the committee will rank teams. I developed this algorithm by combing through the data and seeing which metrics the committee values and which ones aren’t as important. We can get close to approximating how the committee will act, though this year’s group seems willing to shake things up a little more than usual, which makes predicting the rankings more challenging.

Most of the top 16 from last week should feel pretty safe considering only two teams (No. 11 Kentucky and No. 14 Houston) lost. They might not fall far, considering seven of the nine teams ranked from No. 17 to No. 25 lost. That means we could have some losing teams barely falling and/or a handful of new teams entering the rankings. Here’s what my model believes the committee will do:

Next five: LSU, Nebraska, Auburn, UTSA, Arizona

Along with the projected rankings, I’ve included my strength of schedule rankings to this point, strength of record and wins above bubble (wins against a schedule compared to how the average bubble team would perform). These are not exact metrics that the committee uses, but they contextualize how impressive a team’s resume is compared to teams ranked similarly from the model’s perspective.

The three teams directly in front of the Buckeyes in last week’s rankings (South Carolina, USC, Ole Miss) lost, which means Ohio State could move right back into the thick of the bubble conversation after its win over Northwestern. Of course, one of those losing teams, USC, beat Ohio State a few weeks ago, which could limit the Buckeyes’ upward mobility. Will the committee deem those two teams close enough that head-to-head will matter? Or will it bypass the USC victory and push Ohio State higher? My model believes Ohio State will jump ahead of USC because of its advantages in strength of record and wins above bubble metrics.

The model also believes Oregon can jump Iowa after a drubbing of Michigan, a team the Hawkeyes needed a last-second touchdown to beat. The Ducks have one more loss but have faced a tougher schedule, with otherwise comparable resumes. Another data point: Ohio State lost to Oregon but easily beat Iowa.

The Big Ten has had a down year, but suddenly it’s jamming up the bubble. I originally thought three-loss SEC teams would be occupying these spots, but now we’re talking about which Big Ten teams could sneak in.

Texas beat LSU on the road, which makes me wonder whether the Longhorns will get similar treatment to Alabama among two-loss teams. Texas has played the third-toughest schedule in the country, per my model, while having the fourth-best strength of record and second-best wins above bubble rating. That’s an impressive resume that should have Texas in the conversation of jumping ahead of Alabama.

But let’s not get ahead of ourselves after the two were three spots apart last week, with Alabama third and Texas sixth. No. 5 Notre Dame has played the 45th-toughest schedule while having the ninth-best strength of record and eighth-best wins above bubble. Texas at least jumping Notre Dame will be discussed, even if the model doesn’t project it to happen. Personally, I lean against the model here and think Texas gets the nod for a spot in the top five.

No. 13 Wake Forest demolished SMU 49-7 on the road for its most impressive victory of the season. The problem is that No. 12 Texas Tech also had a big victory over Oklahoma State on the road. The Cowboys were ranked in last week’s Top 25, meaning the committee will value that road victory just as much as Wake Forest’s. Maybe No. 10 BYU is the team to fall here, but its win over Notre Dame from earlier in the season is the best win of the trio.

The model doesn’t believe Wake Forest will make up much ground in the rankings this week beyond passing Kentucky, even though it did boost its resume. However, my strength of record and wins above bubble metrics favor Wake Forest in this group, and I believe BYU has the least impressive resume of the three despite the win over the Irish. If you believe Wake Forest is being disrespected, I’m inclined to agree with you if it doesn’t move up more than a spot.

Check back here for the official rankings release after 9 p.m. ET Tuesday.
